hook: The tiny gap that makes or breaks a seal

slides.t: It's the empty space between the food and the jar rim. Every tested recipe tells you exactly how much to leave.
Often 1/4 inch for jams, 1/2 inch for fruit and tomatoes, 1 inch for pressure-canned low-acid foods. Follow the recipe.
Food can bubble out during processing and get under the lid, so the jar may not seal.
Air left in the jar may not all be driven out, which can cause a weak seal and darkened food on top.
A headspace gauge measures the gap. A plastic bubble remover frees trapped air. Then wipe the rim clean.

hook: A gift for the gardener who has everything

slides.t: Soil, cold water and constant washing pull moisture from skin. Gardeners' hands often crack by fall.
A rich cream that soaks in without staying greasy, so it can go on before picking up tools again.
After washing up and at bedtime, when skin has hours to soak it in. Small tubes fit a coat pocket.
Cream plus a good pair of garden gloves is a thoughtful little bundle for any grower.
It's small, useful and gets used every day, which is the best kind of gift.
